• Has exactly two circuit–hyperplanes and these are disjoint.
• The excluded minors for the class of matroids that are binary or ternary are
U2,4 ⊕ F7 , U2,4 ⊕ F7∗ , U2,4 ⊕2 F7 , U2,4 ⊕2 F7∗ , U2,5 , U3,5 , and the unique matroids
obtained by relaxing a circuit–hyperplane in each of AG(3, 2) and T12 (14.5.11).
• Algebraic over F if and only if F has characteristic two.

P G(2, 3)




• The second smallest projective plane; isomorphic to the unique S(2, 3, 13).
• F-representable if and only if F has characteristic three.
• Not graphic, not cographic, not regular, not near-regular.
• Not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• Doubly transitive automorphism group.
• Has every simple ternary matroid of rank at most three as a restriction.
• Algebraic over F if and only if F has characteristic three (Gordon 1988).

M (Wr ), W r




                     The graph Wr , the r-spoked wheel.
• The rank-r wheel and rank-r whirl (r ≥ 2).
• The whirl is the unique relaxation of the wheel.
660                           Some interesting matroids

• M (Wr ) is graphic, cographic, and regular.
• W r is not graphic, not cographic, and not regular; it is F-representable if and
only if |F| ≥ 3, so it is near-regular.
• For r ≥ 3, M (Wr ) is not transversal, not a strict gammoid, and not a gammoid.
• W r is transversal, a strict gammoid, and a gammoid.
• Both are self-dual but not identically self-dual.
• Except for W 2 , which is isomorphic to U2,4 , these matroids have non-transitive
automorphism groups.
• The only 3-connected matroids for which no single-element deletion and no
single-element contraction is 3-connected are the matroids M (Wr ) and W r for
r ≥ 3. The rank-2 whirl W 2 is 3-connected, but M (W2 ) is not.
• Both are algebraic over all fields.
Ur,n
                        E = {1, 2, . . . , n}.
                        B(Ur,n ) = {X ⊆ E : |X| = r}.
                        C(Ur,n ) = {X ⊆ E : |X| = r + 1}.
• The rank-r uniform matroid on an n-element set.
• U2,q+2 and Uq,q+2 are excluded minors for GF (q)-representability. For general
r and n, the F-representability of Ur,n has not been determined (Section 6.5).
• Not graphic, cographic, or regular unless r or n − r is 0 or 1, in which case
Ur,n is graphic, cographic, and regular.
• Transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid.
• Identically self-dual if and only if n = 2r; otherwise not self-dual, the dual
being Un−r,n .
• Automorphism group is the symmetric group.
• Every minor is also uniform.
• 3-connected unless n > 0 and 0 ∈ {r, n − r}, or n > 3 and 1 ∈ {r, n − r}.
• Algebraic over all fields.

P G(r − 1, q)
                                                                    r
• The rank-r projective geometry over GF (q) (Section 6.1); has qq−1 −1
                                                                        elements.
• The simple matroid associated with V (r, q), the r-dimensional vector space
over GF (q).
• P G(−1, q) ∼= U0,0 , P G(0, q) ∼
                                 = U1,1 , and P G(1, q) ∼
                                                        = U2,q+1 .
• For r ≥ 3, F-representable if and only if F has GF (q) as a subfield.
• For r ≥ 3, not graphic, not cographic, not regular.
• For r ≥ 3, not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• For r ≥ 3, never self-dual.
• For r ≤ 2, automorphism group is the symmetric group; for r ≥ 3, automor-
phism group is doubly transitive.
• Every simple GF (q)-representable matroid of rank at most r is a restriction of
P G(r − 1, q).
                             Some interesting matroids                                661

• The restriction to every flat is isomorphic to P G(k − 1, q) for some k ≤ r.
• The simple matroid associated with every proper contraction is isomorphic to
P G(k − 1, q) for some k < r.
• For r ≥ 3, algebraic over F if and only if F and GF (q) have the same charac-
teristic.

AG(r − 1, q)
• The rank-r affine geometry over GF (q); has q r−1 elements when r ≥ 1.
• Obtained by deleting a hyperplane from P G(r − 1, q).
• AG(−1, q) ∼ = U0,0 , AG(0, q) ∼ = U1,1 , and AG(1, q) ∼  = U2,q .
• AG(2, 2) ∼   U
            = 3,4  ; for AG(2,  3) see above. For   r = 3  and q ≥ 4, and for r ≥ 4,
AG(r − 1, q) is F-representable if and only if F has GF (q) as a subfield.
• For r, q ≥ 3, not graphic, not cographic, not regular.
• For r, q ≥ 3, not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• For r ≥ 3, identically self-dual if and only if (r − 1, q) = (3, 2); otherwise never
self-dual.
• For r ≤ 2 or (r − 1, q) = (2, 2), automorphism group is the symmetric group.
In all other cases, automorphism group is doubly transitive.
• The restriction to every flat is isomorphic to AG(k − 1, q) for some k ≤ r.
• The simple matroid associated with every proper contraction is isomorphic to
P G(k − 1, q) for some k < r.
• 3-connected unless (r − 1, q) is (1, 2) or (2, 2).
• For r = 3 and q ≥ 5, and for r ≥ 4, the matroid AG(r − 1, q) is algebraic over
F if and only if F has the same characteristic as GF (q).

                                           1 0 1       ···    1     1

                   This matrix represents Zr over GF (2).
• Defined for all r ≥ 3; the unique rank-r binary spike with tip t (12.2.20).
• Z3 \e ∼                        = F7 ; Z4 \t ∼
         = M (K4 ) for all e; Z3 ∼              = AG(3, 2); Z4 \e ∼   = S8 for all e = t.
• Zr \t, the tipless binary spike, is self-dual; it is identically self-dual if and only
if r is even.
• F-representable if and only if F has characteristic two.
• Not graphic, not cographic, not regular, not near-regular.
• Not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• For all e and f in E(Zr ) − t, there is an automorphism of Zr that fixes t and
interchanges e and f , so Zr \t has a transitive automorphism group.
662                              Some interesting matroids

• For all e = t, the matroid Zr \e is self-dual but not identically self-dual.
• For r ≥ 4, every single-element contraction of Zr \t is isomorphic to Zr−1 .
• A 3-connected binary matroid of rank at least three has no M (W4 )-minor if
and only if it is isomorphic to Zr , Zr∗ , Zr \t, or Zr \yr for some r ≥ 3 (12.2.21).
• Algebraic over F if and only if F has characteristic two.

r-spike
E = {t, x1 , x2 , . . . , xr , y1 , y2 , . . . , yr } and r(E) = r.
Li = {t, xi , yi } is a circuit for all i.
For 1 ≤ k ≤ r − 1, the union of any k of L1 , L2 , . . . , Lr has rank k + 1.
• Defined for all r ≥ 3; a rank-r spike with tip t and legs L1 , L2 , . . . , Lr . Deleting
t gives a tipless rank-r spike.
• The non-spanning circuits are L1 , L2 , . . . , Lr , all sets of the form (Li ∪ Lj ) − t
for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ r, and some (possibly empty) collection C3 of sets of the form
{z1 , z2 , . . . , zr } where zi ∈ {xi , yi } for all i and no two members of C3 have more
than r − 2 common elements.
• For r ≥ 4, the members of C3 are the circuit–hyperplanes of the spike.
• When C3 is empty, the spike is free.
• Each of F7 , F7− , and P7 is a 3-spike.
• The collection of spikes includes infinite antichains that are non-representable
(14.1.3) and that are representable over every infinite field (14.3.15).
• The free r-spike is representable over all sufficiently large fields and over GF (pk )
for all primes p and all k ≥ 2. For such p and k, when pk ≥ 8, the free r-spike
has at least 2r−1 inequivalent GF (pk )-representations (14.6.8).
• The free r-spike is obtained by truncating the parallel connection of r copies
of U2,3 across a common basepoint.
• Not graphic, not cographic, not regular.
• Not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• Deleting any element gives a self-dual matroid. The tipless free spike is iden-
tically self-dual.
• Every spike is 3-connected and has branch-width three (14.3.14).
• A rank-r matroid M on a 2r-element set E is a tipless spike if and only if there
is a partition of E into r pairs of elements such that the union of every two such
pairs is both a circuit and a cocircuit of M (2.1.28)
• For r ≥ 4, deleting the tip and contracting any other element gives an (r − 1)-
spike.
• Among r-spikes, exactly one is binary, exactly two are ternary, and exactly
(r2 + 6r + 24)/12 are quaternary (Wu 2003).
• The free r-spike is algebraic over all fields.
                             Some interesting matroids                                663

Qr (A)
• The rank-r Dowling
                      geometry associated with the finite group A (Section 6.10).
• Has r + |A| r2 elements including a distinguished basis whose members are
called joints; the matroid obtained by deleting
                                                      these joints is Qr (A), the joint-
                                           r
less Dowling geometry, which has |A| 2 elements.
• Qr (A) has rank r unless |A| = 1 and r ≥ 1 in which case its rank is r − 1.
• Q0 (A) ∼= U0,0 ; Q1 (A) ∼
                          = U1,1 ; and Q2 (A) ∼   = U2,|A|+2 .
• Qr (GF (2)× ) ∼= M (Kr+1 ) and Qr (GF (2)× ) ∼    = M (Kr ).
• Qr (GF (q)× ) is represented over GF (q) by a matrix whose columns consist of
all vectors with one or two non-zero entries, the first of which is a one.
• Q3 (GF (3)× ) ∼
                 = M (K4 ) and Q3 (GF (4)× ) ∼ = AG(2, 3).
• For r ≥ 3, the matroid Qr (A) is F-representable if and only if A is isomorphic
to a subgroup of F× (6.10.10).
• For |A| = 1, graphic and regular; cographic if and only if r ≤ 3. For |A| ≥ 2
and r ≥ 3, not graphic, not cographic, not regular.
• For |A| ≥ 2 and r ≥ 3, not sixth-root-of-unity, not near-regular; dyadic if and
only if |A| = 2.
• For r ≥ 3, not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• Self-dual if and only if (r, |A|) ∈ {(0, |A|), (2, 2), (3, 1)}; identically self-dual if
and only if (r, |A|) ∈ {(0, |A|), (2, 2)}.
• For r ≥ 3, if Qr (A) ∼= Qr (A ), then A ∼  = A .
• For all r ≥ 1, the simple matroid associated with every single-element contrac-
tion is isomorphic to Qr−1 (A).
• The restriction of Qr (A) to a flat is isomorphic to the direct sum of the cycle
matroids of a family of complete graphs and Qk (A) for some k ≤ r.
• For r ≤ 2, automorphism group is the symmetric group; for |A| = 1, auto-
morphism group is transitive; otherwise, automorphism group is not transitive
although if e and f are both joints or are both non-joints, there is an automor-
phism that interchanges them.
• Has exactly ((|A| + 1)r − 1)/|A| hyperplanes.

Θn
E = X ∪ Y where X = {x1 , x2 , . . . , xn } and Y = {y1 , y2 , . . . , yn }.
B(Θn ) = {B ⊆ E : |B| = n; |B ∩ X| ≤ 2; B = (Y − yi ) ∪ xi for all i}.
• Defined for all n ≥ 2; the circuits consist of all 3-element subsets of X, all sets
of the form (Y − yi ) ∪ xi , and all sets of the form (Y − yu ) ∪ {xs , xt } where s, t,
and u are distinct.
• Θ2 ∼= U1,2 ⊕ U1,2 and Θ3 ∼  = M (K4 ).
• F-representable if and only if |F| ≥ n − 1.
• For n ≤ 3, graphic, cographic, and regular; for n = 4, not graphic, not co-
graphic, not regular, near-regular; for n ≥ 5, not graphic, not cographic, not
regular, not near-regular.
664                             Some interesting matroids

• For n ≥ 3, not transversal, not a strict gammoid, not a gammoid.
• Self-dual; identically self-dual if and only if n = 2.
• Has X as a modular flat.
• For a matroid M with E(M ) ∩ (X ∪ Y ) = X and X a coindependent set in M
with M |X ∼ = U2,n , a segment–cosegment exchange on X is PX (Θn , M )\X.
• The set of excluded minors for F-representability is closed under segment–
cosegment exchange and its dual operation, cosegment–segment exchange (11.5.15).
• For n ≥ 3, a 3-connected matroid.
• Θn /yi \xi ∼
             = Θn−1 for all n ≥ 3 and for all i.
• For n ≤ 3, automorphism group is transitive; for n ≥ 4, automorphism group
has X and Y as its orbits.
• Algebraic over all fields.

Ψr

E = {a1 , b1 , a2 , b2 , . . . , ar , br } and r(E) = r. Non-spanning circuits are
all the sets {ai , bi , zi+1 , zi+2 , . . . , zi+k−1 , ai+k , bi+k } for 1 ≤ k ≤ r − 3,
where each zj is in {aj , bj }, and all subscripts are calculated mod r.
• The rank-r free swirl; defined for all r ≥ 3.
• Ψ3 ∼= U3,6 .
• The matroid obtained from the rank-r whirl by freely adding an element on
each 3-point line is the rank-r jointed free swirl, Ψ+ r . Deleting all the spokes of
the whirl from Ψ+  r gives Ψ r .
• Not binary, not ternary.
• Ψ3 is F-representable if and only if |F| ≥ 4, while Ψ+  3 is F-representable if and
only if |F| ≥ 5.
• When r ≥ 4, the matroids Ψr and Ψ+      r are representable over exactly the same
fields; Ψr is representable over all infinite fields and over all GF (q) with q ≥ 4
unless q = 2p where 2p − 1 is prime. In the exceptional case, Ψr is not GF (q)-
representable for all sufficiently large r (14.6.7).
• When q > 5 and q is not of the form 2p where 2p − 1 is prime, Ψ+     r has at least
2r inequivalent GF (q)-representations.
• Not graphic, not cographic, not regular, not near-regular.
• Transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid.
• Identically self-dual.
• Transitive automorphism group.
• 3-connected but, for all r ≥ 4, not 4-connected.
• The elements ai and bi are clones for all i.
• Algebraic over all fields.
